title.narrative: Spotlight Initiative - Gender Transformative Joint Programme for the Promotion of Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment: Towards the Elimination of Gender Based Violence

description.narrative: Outcome A: Legislative, policy, and data frameworks on GEWE and EVAWG are strengthened, operationalized through multi-sectoral plans, and implemented at national and sub-national levels. Within this outcome, the programme will strengthen capacity across civil society and government actors to coordinate, advocate, develop, implement, monitor and evaluate policies and legislation on gender equality and GBV and develop gender-responsive budgets. There shall be comprehensive assessment of legislative landscape in relation to GEWE and EVAWG across sectors (including statutory and customary laws, institutions and stakeholders). Integrating the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (ACRWC) into a comprehensive assessment of the legislative landscape concerning Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment (GEWE) and Ending Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) in Zambia is crucial for a holistic approach. The assessment will analyse how domestic laws align with the specific articles of the ACRWC, particularly those related to protection from violence, abuse, and exploitation, and highlight discrepancies or gaps. The outcome also will promote knowledge, understanding and commitment on National Gender Policy among GRZ Permanent Secretaries and Directors in addition to establishing or strengthening inclusive engagement platforms with women’s rights organisations to inform GRZ policy processes; The outputs have been locally adapted and will relate to the global menu “National and regional partners have strengthened evidence-based knowledge and capacities to assess gaps and draft new and/or strengthen existing legislations on ending VAWG and/or gender equality and non-discrimination that respond to the rights of the most groups facing multiple and intersecting forms of discrimination and are in line with international HR standards and treaty bodies’ recommendations”. There will also be building the capacity of key stakeholders (government, women’s rights organisations, traditional and faith leaders) to design, implement and monitor gender equitable policies; Support the implementation and monitoring of GEWE and EVAWG laws and policies at national and sub-national levels (e.g., school re-entry policy guidelines for the girls who fall pregnant and have to leave).
